REQ-1-1-1.name: Register a New GitHub Account
REQ-1-1-1.description:
The registration page is the form opened by the unique link named “Create an account” from the sign-in page. The form contains exactly one textbox labeled “Username”, one textbox labeled “Email”, one password input labeled “Password”, one password input labeled “Confirm password”, one initially unchecked checkbox named “Agree to the terms”, and one enabled button named “Create account”. The username and email identify the account, while passwords must not be echoed on the page. This product directly marks the email of a successfully registered account as verified and does not provide a subsequent email-verification page. The visitor enters a unique username, email, password, and matching confirmation, checks “Agree to the terms”, and activates “Create account”. The username must consist of 1 to 39 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, or single hyphens (`-`) and must not begin or end with a hyphen; after trimming leading and trailing whitespace, the email must contain exactly one `@`, be no longer than 254 characters, and have at least one dot and non-empty domain labels after the `@`; the password must contain 12 to 128 characters, include at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit, and one non-alphanumeric special character, and contain no whitespace characters. The system stores a sign-in-capable account together with its verified-email status and enters the sign-in page; if the username or email conflicts, any field is missing, the email format is invalid, the terms are not accepted, the password is noncompliant, or the confirmation does not match, the system retains the username and email input, displays an itemized message beside the corresponding field, and does not create an account. The corresponding visible field message contains “Username already exists”, “Username format is invalid”, “Email format is invalid”, “Password requirements are not satisfied”, or “Agree to terms is required”, as applicable. Visitors can use this capability on the account-access page. The system validates input rules, displays field errors, and prevents duplicate accounts; on success, it directly creates an available account. Submitting several invalid fields together must show the username, email, password, and missing-terms messages together, rather than revealing only one error per submission; the submit button remains actionable so these messages can be read. For example, a username beginning with a hyphen, email “not-an-email”, password “short”, confirmation “different”, and unchecked terms produce these field errors and preserve the attempted username. A duplicate username paired with a different unused email displays “Username already exists” and retains both attempted values. A successful registration accepts a unique username such as “pw-user-<unique suffix>”, its “@example.test” email, and password “Valid-password-123!”; the sign-in form is immediately available, accepts that email, and the resulting signed-in username remains visible after reload.

Screenshot reference:
![image](reference/github-sign-up.png)

The visitor enters a compliant 1–39-character username, a compliant email, a compliant 12–128-character password, and an identical confirmation password, checks the terms-agreement checkbox, and clicks “Create account”. Seed values: account `alice-dev`, email `alice.dev@example.test`, password `Valid-password-123!`.

The system displays registration success and redirects to the sign-in page without displaying the password; the account's email can now be used for sign-in and password recovery. If the username, email, any required field, terms, or password rules are not satisfied, the system remains on the registration page, displays the reason beside the corresponding field, retains the username and email input, and does not create an account. The visitor can immediately sign in with the new account and enter the workspace; after a failed submission, reopening the registration page shows that no new account corresponding to the failed input exists. REQ-1-1-2.name: Sign In with an Existing Account
REQ-1-1-2.description:
This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-1-1-1 (Register a New GitHub Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. The sign-in page is the form on the account-access page containing “Username or email”, “Password”, and “Sign in”. A “session” is the current-browser login record saved after successful account authentication, represented in the frontend by the upper-right account menu and access to protected pages. The visitor enters a username or email and a password and submits the form. The system looks up the account and validates its credentials and availability status; if authentication fails due to an unknown username/email, incorrect password, or unavailable account, the system displays exactly the same generic failure message “Invalid credentials”, does not disclose whether the account exists or which credential was wrong, and does not create a session. After successful authentication, the system stores a session with a unique session identifier, account identifier, and active status, then redirects to the workspace accessible to that user; the session remains valid after refreshing or reopening the workspace, and subsequent protected organization, repository, and work-item requests must use this session to determine the current user.

![image](reference/github-sign-in.png)

REQ-2-1-1.name: Browse Organization Repositories
REQ-2-1-1.description:
The organization page presents “Repositories” as a navigation link, visually usable as a tab, and a textbox labeled “Find a repository”. Filtering updates the visible results as the user types, without a separate submit action. Each result has a link named exactly with the repository name, and opens a heading displaying “organization name/repository name”. Returning with browser Back keeps the public result available; filtering by the exact private repository name never exposes its link to a visitor. The seed organization has a public repository and a distinct private repository inaccessible to visitors. From the organization page, the user clicks the “Repositories” link, can enter a repository name in the filter box, select a public/private filter, and click a repository name in the list to open its overview. The system displays only the names, descriptions, visibility, and update times of repositories visible to the current user; clicking a result opens that repository's overview. Visitors can view public repositories on a public organization overview page; signed-in accounts can see only repositories for which they have read permission on the Repositories tab of the organization overview. The list reads repository name, description, visibility, and update time and provides no write operations; private repositories must first be validated under the already defined repository-access rules.

Screenshot reference:
![image](reference/github-organization-repositories.png)

Seed values: organization `Acme Demo`, repository `acme-docs`, member `bob-reviewer`, team `frontend-team`.

REQ-2-1-2.name: Create an Organization After Authentication
REQ-2-1-2.description: The account-menu link “Your organizations” opens a page with the link “New organization”. Its form has fields labeled “Organization name” and “Display name” and a button “Create organization”. The new overview uses a heading containing the organization identifier, which remains after reload. Submitting an existing identifier must show “Organization name already exists” even when the display name is also missing; it must not navigate to a heading for the existing organization. The malformed identifier “-invalid-organization” and a whitespace-only display name are rejected with the applicable field error. Seed data supplies a verified creator and an existing organization identifier for the duplicate case. A signed-in user enters a unique organization name and display information on the organization-creation page and confirms. The organization name must comply with the 1–39-character lowercase ASCII REQ-1 username format and be globally unique; the display name must contain 1–100 non-empty characters after trimming leading and trailing whitespace. The system validates these rules, creates the organization identifier, display name, and creation time, and saves the current user as both initial owner and member; if the name or display name is noncompliant, the name conflicts, or persistence fails, the system retains non-sensitive input, displays the reason in the corresponding field, and does not create the organization. The applicable visible message is “Organization name already exists”, “Organization name format is invalid”, or “Display name is required”. On success, the user is redirected to the new organization overview page, the organization appears in the current user's accessible-organization list, and subsequent team, member, and repository authorization is scoped by that organization identifier. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

REQ-2-2-3.name: Directly Add a User as an Organization Member
REQ-2-2-3.description: The organization overview opens “People” through a link. Its button “Add member” opens the labeled field “Username or email”, a combobox “Role” defaulting to Member, and a submission button “Add member”. Opening Role exposes clickable options “Member” and “Owner”. If the opening button remains present, the form submission button follows it in page order. The successful People list displays the full target username and Member role, with no Pending or Awaiting state; reload preserves the row. On duplicate or unknown-account failure, keep the form open so the username can be corrected and resubmitted; the existing member's complete username appears only once in the People list. A separately signed-in new member sees the organization identifier as complete visible text in Your organizations, while an ungranted private repository shows “Access denied”. The scenarios provide an Owner, a registered nonmember, a different existing member, an unknown username, and a private organization repository with no direct or team grant to the new member. On the “People” page, an organization Owner clicks “Add member”, enters the username or verified email of an existing account, selects “Member” or “Owner”, and clicks “Add member”. The system atomically stores the “organization-account-role” membership relationship and immediately displays the organization in both the People list and the target account's “Your organizations” list; the target account can see the organization on its next sign-in, after refreshing the workspace, or after reopening the organization overview. A Member gains only organization visibility and eligibility to become a candidate for team/repository authorization; an Owner additionally gains Admin permission over the organization and its repositories. For an existing member, unknown account, unsupported role, or persistence failure, the system displays the reason and does not change the membership relationship; an existing member displays “Account is already a member”, and the unknown username `unknown-reviewer` displays “Account not found”. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-2-1-2 (Create an Organization After Authentication); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

REQ-2-2-4.name: Remove a Member from an Organization
REQ-2-2-4.description: Open the organization's “People” link to read member usernames. Each removable member has a button named “Member menu <username>”; it opens the menuitem “Remove from organization”, followed by the confirmation button “Remove”. Successful removal makes the complete username absent from People immediately and after reload. A non-Owner viewing the same member has no member-menu button and no Remove from organization menuitem, rather than merely a disabled control. Each independent scenario starts with that member present; the non-Owner is an ordinary organization member. On the “People” page, an organization Owner locates a member, clicks “Remove from organization” in that member's action menu, and clicks “Remove” in the confirmation dialog. The system atomically deletes that member's organization-membership relationship, all of the account's memberships in teams of that organization, and all direct grants to that account on repositories of the organization; if the account still obtains repository permission through another organization Owner status or an undeleted team grant, effective permission is recalculated according to the valid permission rules, otherwise access is denied. The system must not delete the personal account, personal repositories, relationships with other organizations, teams themselves, or team grants; the last Owner must not be removed. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-2-1-2 (Create an Organization After Authentication); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

REQ-3-2-1.name: Create a Repository with Owner, Visibility, and Initialization Options
REQ-3-2-1.description:
This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. The signed-in workspace provides a “New repository” link. The form labels are “Owner”, “Repository name”, and “Description”; the signed-in user's personal namespace is selected by default, so it is possible to submit without changing the owner. Visibility choices are radio controls “Public” and “Private”; initialization is a checkbox “Add a README file”; submission uses the button “Create repository”. Other defaults must allow duplicate-name and empty-name validation without further input. A successful initialized private repository shows a heading containing the new name, a visible Private marker, and a README file link; the overview persists after reload. The optional description “Repository created by Playwright” is saved when entered. An existing repository in this same default personal namespace is supplied for duplicate validation, which stays on the form and does not open the existing repository heading. On the repository-creation page, a signed-in user selects a personal or organization owner, enters a repository name and description, selects public or private visibility, and chooses whether to create an initial commit with a README. The system verifies that the user may create a repository in that owner's namespace, that the name is unique, and that the options are valid; on success, it stores the repository identifier, owner, visibility, default branch, and creator. If initialization is selected, it must also atomically create the initial branch, README file, and initial commit; failure at any step must leave no partially created repository. On success, the new repository overview page is opened.

REQ-4-2-3.name: Search Code Within a Repository
REQ-4-2-3.description:
The user enters a code keyword in the search box at the top of the repository page and presses Enter, selects the “Code” results page, can further filter by path or language, and clicks a matching file. The system displays matching snippets, file paths, and branch/revision context within the visible code scope of the current repository; clicking a result opens the corresponding file location. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-4-1 (Browse Repository Files and Directories); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. Visitors can search from the Code page of a public repository, while signed-in accounts can search any repository they are authorized to view; the results page only reads file content, matching snippets, and paths from currently visible branches of the current repository and cannot leak results across repositories or write code. The repository page and search results expose one searchbox named “Search”; after Enter, a unique link named “Code” selects code results. This results-type link must remain distinguishable from repository navigation so the active search page has only one Code link. Path and language filters are optional, and an unfiltered search can immediately open a result link whose exact accessible name is the matching file name. Seed data provides the known query `search flow`, a matching file `README.md` with that query visible as a complete text value, and the absent query `no-such-token`, which does not occur in searchable code. Opening the matching file shows that text; refreshing preserves the file context, text, and a link named exactly after the file. For the absent query, show “No code results” and retain the exact query in Search. Returning to the repository and repeating the same search produces the same empty state without stale matches.

REQ-4-3-3.name: Change the Repository Default Branch
REQ-4-3-3.description:
A repository administrator enters “Settings” → “Branches”, selects an existing branch from the “Default branch” dropdown, clicks “Update”, and then confirms the change. The system saves the new default branch and updates the initial branch shown when the repository is newly opened; it does not delete or rewrite the previous default branch. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-4-3-1 (List and Switch Repository Branches) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. Only a repository Admin or organization Owner may change the default branch on repository code and version-control pages; other roles may only view. The system validates the role, stores the new default branch together with the operator and time, and rejects unauthorized requests. “Settings” and “Branches” are unique links on their respective pages; “Default branch” is a native HTML select element exposing the combobox role, with options labeled by exact existing branch names; selecting an option must use the native selection behavior. The administrator selects a different seeded branch, activates the “Update” button, and then the “Confirm” button in the confirmation dialog. Opening the repository page entry without a branch then shows “Branch <new default branch name>”; opening that selector still offers an option named exactly after the old default branch. A non-Admin may have Settings or Branches links hidden or may open a read-only settings page, but no “Default branch” combobox or default-branch update button is rendered for that user; a merely disabled editable selector is insufficient.

REQ-4-4.name: Manage Repository Files Through the Web Interface
REQ-4-4.description:
This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-4-1 (Browse Repository Files and Directories) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. The file editor is the form opened from Edit or Add file on the Code page; the user edits file content at a path on the current branch and submits it. Only Write, Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may submit; Read and Triage may only view. A single submission stores the file-path and content change, commit message, author, parent commit, and target branch as one indivisible record and moves the target branch to point to that new commit. A new or renamed file path must not be empty, must not begin with `/`, must not contain a `..` path segment, and must not conflict with an existing file or directory on the current branch; the commit message must contain 1–72 non-empty characters after trimming leading and trailing whitespace. If the path conflicts, content validation fails, the commit message is noncompliant, the branch is protected, or persistence fails, the page displays the reason and does not change the file, branch head, or commit history. An invalid path displays “Invalid file path”, and an empty commit message displays “Commit message is required”. From the writable Code page, the unique “Add file” button opens the “Create new file” menuitem. The editor has a field labeled “File name”, a textbox named “File contents”, an initially empty field labeled “Commit message”, and a “Commit changes” button. Creating a unique file such as `pw-file-<unique suffix>.md` with nonempty text and a message such as `Add <file name>` immediately opens a view displaying the exact saved content. Its “Commits” link opens history displaying the exact submitted message. Submitting `../invalid.md` with content `must not be saved` and no commit message reports the invalid path and/or required message and changes neither files nor history. The example content is ordinary text, not a forbidden content value by itself; rejection follows from the invalid path or missing message.

![image](reference/github-web-file-editor.png)

REQ-5-4.name: Close or Reopen an Issue
REQ-5-4.description: Only users with Triage, Maintain, or Admin may close or reopen an issue from the issue detail view; Write and Read users may only view the status. The system stores the Open or Closed status, operator, and time, records the transition in activity history, and shows it to subsequent viewers; the status transition must not modify the title, description, comments, labels, assignees, or milestone. The closable seed issue starts Open. The detail page offers a “Close issue” button when Open and a “Reopen issue” button when Closed; activating either immediately saves the change without an additional confirmation. Closing displays Closed status and a “Closed issue” activity, and reopening displays Open status. After reopening and reload the “Close issue” button is available again. On the separate protected issue, the Read viewer sees neither close nor reopen button; hiding both controls is required, in addition to rejecting unauthorized requests. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-5-1-2 (View an Issue and Its Discussion); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

REQ-6-3-1.name: View Pull Request Overview and Commits
REQ-6-3-1.description: The PR detail page is the unified read view for the same PR number. A seeded public Open PR is directly viewable without sign-in and displays its exact title in a heading. Commits and Files changed are links; the Commits view displays a Commit summary, and the Files changed view displays a Changed files summary. Reloading preserves the heading and usable navigation links; leaving and reopening the same visible page restores the same PR and allows the same navigation. Seed data includes its stable title, description, discussion comment, and at least one comparable commit. Conversation is the timeline for the author's description, ordinary comments, review summaries, and status events; Commits is the list of commits on the PR's current compare branch relative to base; Files changed is the entry point to the current diff. Users with repository-view permission can switch among the three tabs; all read the same persisted PR, branch, and commit data and do not create comments, reviews, or merges. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-2-3 (Create a Pull Request from Comparison Results); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

REQ-6-3-2.name: Inspect Changed Files and Aggregate Diff
REQ-6-3-2.description: Files changed is the read-only diff view on a PR detail page computed from the current base and compare commits. From a visible public pull request entry, a visitor activates the Files changed link and sees the known changed file path verbatim and visible aggregate text such as 3 additions, 1 deletions. This public PR seed contains the same known changed-file path `src/search.ts` supplied for branch comparison, with one added file and one modified file; it requires no sign-in. Each diff block displays the file path and added/deleted lines; aggregate statistics show the current PR's number of changed files and line counts in the format “<addition count> additions, <deletion count> deletions”. Users with repository-view permission may expand files or navigate to lines, but this operation does not modify files, commits, branches, comments, or review status. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-3-1 (View Pull Request Overview and Commits); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

REQ-6-4.name: Request or Remove Pull Request Reviewers
REQ-6-4.description: The Reviewers button opens a picker with a textbox named Search. Typing an eligible username immediately reveals an option with that exact accessible name. Selecting the option saves the request immediately without a separate Save action, closes the picker, and displays the username in the reviewer area; it remains after reload. Each requested reviewer has a button named Remove followed by a space and the username; clicking it immediately removes the request and the username from that area, without a confirmation step. The seed PR is Open, belongs to the signed-in author, and initially has no request or submitted review from the eligible target reviewer; the target is a distinct non-author collaborator with Write or higher permission. Removing a request persists across reload. A “reviewer request” is a pending-review relationship between a PR and a candidate reviewer account, displayed in the Reviewers area on the right side of the PR detail page; it is not the same as a submitted review decision. The author of an Open or Draft PR, Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may create or delete this relationship. Matching reviewer options update as the user types in the search textbox; pressing Enter or activating a separate search button is not required before selecting an option. A candidate reviewer must have Write, Maintain, or Admin on the repository and must not be the PR author; the system stores or deletes the “PR-reviewer request” relationship together with the operator and time. Removing a request does not delete reviews, comments, or activity records already submitted by that user and does not change the user's effective review decision. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-2-3 (Create a Pull Request from Comparison Results) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

REQ-6-5.name: Merge an Eligible Pull Request
REQ-6-5.description: On an eligible PR, Merge pull request and then Confirm merge are buttons; confirming displays Merged, and that state remains after reload. A blocked PR keeps a visible disabled Merge pull request button and explains its unmet review or protection condition before any click. Seed data supplies a Maintain account and separate Open PRs for success and refusal. The eligible PR targets protected main, has a current non-author approval and test: success, and has no conflicts. The blocked PR targets a protected branch and lacks the required valid approval; its disabled button is accompanied by Review required by branch protection. Each seed state is restored independently before reuse. “Merge” is the only write operation that writes the current compare commit's changes from an Open PR into the base branch; it is not simply marking the PR as complete. Only Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may merge from the PR detail page using the sole supported “Create a merge commit” method; the merge confirmation area should display satisfied and unsatisfied conditions. Before confirmation, the system rereads the target branch head, current compare commit, merge-conflict state, and protection rules — there must be no valid Request changes; if the target is protected, each enabled rule requirement is enforced independently, requiring 1 valid non-author Approve for the current compare commit when Require 1 approval is enabled and requiring `test` success when Require status check test is enabled. An unprotected target has no additional approval-count or check-success requirement, but merging still requires no merge conflicts and no valid Request changes review. After validation succeeds, the system atomically creates a merge commit whose parents are the target-branch head at merge time and the current compare commit, updates the target-branch head, sets the PR to Merged, and stores the merger, time, and resulting commit identifier. If any condition is unsatisfied or persistence fails, the page explains the applicable reason and neither the target branch nor PR changes; a missing required approval displays “Review required by branch protection”. Merged is terminal. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-3-4 (Submit a Pull Request Review) and REQ-6-1 (Protect Branches with Review and Status-Check Requirements); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

After refreshing the PR and `main` branch, the merged status and resulting commit remain; if the PR is a draft, lacks approval, has a failed check, is unmergeable, or the user lacks permission, the merge entry is disabled or rejected and the target branch and PR state remain unchanged.
